standard_prerequisites.name: Localization at an idempotent splits a ring as a product of the localization at the idempotent and the quotient by the ideal generated by it
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: used at proof lines 32015-32018, where C'_{f_i} = A_{f_i}/(e_i) and the decomposition B = B_e times B/(e) for an idempotent e is applied
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the localization of the constructed component C' at each generator with the complementary factor of C_{f_i}, which is what produces the product C times C'.

standard_prerequisites.name: An idempotent of a localization A_f can be written in the form a/f^n, and the representative can be adjusted so that it is itself an idempotent after multiplying by a power of f
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: used at proof lines 31997-32001, where e_i = a_i/f_i^n is written and the relation a_i^2 = f_i^n a_i is arranged
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the elements a_i in A whose ideal defines C' and makes the comparison of the two components at f_i computable.

standard_prerequisites.name: If two elements agree after inverting f_i f_j for all i and j then they agree after inverting the product of the generators, and an isomorphism that holds after localizing at f_1, ..., f_r holds after localizing at any element of the ideal they generate
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the bounded relations (f_i f_j a_j)^N (f_j^n a_i - f_i^n a_j) = 0 and, at the end, transfers the isomorphism from the generators to every element of I.

core_obligations: Choose generators f_1, ..., f_r of I, write C_{f_i} = (A_{f_i})_{e_i} for idempotents e_i, express each as e_i = a_i/f_i^n with a common n, and arrange after enlarging n that a_i^2 = f_i^n a_i for every i (proof lines 31992-32001).

Use the compatibility of the idempotents over the localizations at f_i f_j to produce, after enlarging n again, relations showing that f_i^n a_j lies in the ideal generated by a_i for every pair i, j (proof lines 32002-32012).
Define C' = A/(a_1, ..., a_r) and verify that C'_{f_i} = A_{f_i}/(a_i) = A_{f_i}/(e_i), so that at each generator the ring splits as the product of C_{f_i} and C'_{f_i} (proof lines 32013-32019).

Transfer the conclusion from the generators to arbitrary f in I: since the f_i generate the unit ideal in A_f, the map A_f -> (C times C')_f is an isomorphism if and only if it is one after localizing at each f_i, which holds by the previous step (proof lines 32019-32026).
proof_roadmap: Extract idempotents e_i describing C over each generator and realize them by elements a_i with a_i^2 = f_i^n a_i for a common exponent (proof lines 31992-32001).
Compare the idempotents over the pairwise localizations and, after enlarging the exponent, arrange that f_i^n a_j lies in the ideal of a_i for all i, j (proof lines 32002-32012).
Set C' = A/(a_1, ..., a_r), split A_{f_i} as C_{f_i} times C'_{f_i} at each generator and glue along the generators to conclude for every element of I (proof lines 32013-32026).
difficulty_reason: The statement is a glueing lemma over the open pieces of a finitely generated ideal: given a ring map A -> C that becomes localization at an idempotent after inverting each element of a finitely generated ideal I, it produces a surjection A -> C' such that A_f -> (C times C')_f is an isomorphism for every f in I (statement lines 31983-31990). The proof is a concrete calculation with idempotents: it lifts the idempotents e_i of the localizations to elements a_i of A satisfying a_i^2 = f_i^n a_i for a common exponent, uses the compatibility of the idempotents over the pairwise localizations to force f_i^n a_j into the ideal of a_i after enlarging the exponent, defines C' as the quotient by the ideal generated by the a_i, and checks the splitting at each generator before transferring to all of I (proof lines 31992-32026). The non-routine part is exactly the exponent bookkeeping that makes all the a_i comparable at once. The final transfer uses a labelled lemma of another chapter as a pointer for the glueing of the local isomorphisms; the construction and all computations are inside the counted span.
